candidates.name: Tuberculous osteomyelitis
support_spans: He had been receiving anti-tubercular therapy for presumed pulmonary tuberculosis for 6 months
Magnetic resonance imaging of the right shoulder and left ankle demonstrated findings consistent with osteomyelitis involving the scapula and the distal tibia
An aspiration of the scapular swelling was performed, and specimens were sent for culture, sensitivity testing, and histopathologic examination for possible multidrug-resistant tuberculosis
candidates.why: The patient's history of anti-tubercular therapy and the presence of osteomyelitis suggest tuberculous osteomyelitis.

candidates.name: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis
support_spans: He had been receiving anti-tubercular therapy for presumed pulmonary tuberculosis for 6 months; the diagnosis had been based on cough, chest radiograph findings, and an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, with negative sputum studies.
An aspiration of the scapular swelling was performed, and specimens were sent for culture, sensitivity testing, and histopathologic examination for possible multidrug-resistant tuberculosis.
candidates.why: The patient's lack of response to anti-tubercular therapy and the presence of osteomyelitis suggest multidrug-resistant tuberculosis.

candidates.name: Chronic osteomyelitis due to pyogenic bacteria
support_spans: Laboratory studies showed an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 73 mm/h and a positive C-reactive protein level of 96 mg/L
Magnetic resonance imaging of the right shoulder and left ankle demonstrated findings consistent with osteomyelitis involving the scapula and the distal tibia
contradict_spans: He had been receiving anti-tubercular therapy for presumed pulmonary tuberculosis for 6 months

selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of pain and swelling around the right scapula, along with MRI findings consistent with osteomyelitis, strongly support Tuberculous osteomyelitis. The fact that the patient was already receiving anti-tubercular therapy and developed new symptoms suggests possible multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, but the direct evidence of osteomyelitis makes Tuberculous osteomyelitis a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pulmonary tuberculosis
rejected.why: While the patient was initially diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis, the current symptoms and findings are more consistent with osteomyelitis, making pulmonary tuberculosis less relevant to the current presentation.
